# tag: coding.python.builtins
what does abs do in python | python abs function | how do i use abs() in python => abs(x) gives the distance from zero, so abs(-7) is 7 and abs(3.5) is 3.5.
what does all do in python | python all function | how do i use all() in python => all(items) is True if every item is truthy (or the list is empty), like all([1, 2, 3]). One falsy item makes it False.
what does any do in python | python any function | how do i use any() in python => any(items) is True if at least one item is truthy, like any([0, 0, 5]). An empty list gives False.
what does bin do in python | python bin function | how do i use bin() in python => bin(n) turns a whole number into a binary string, so bin(5) is '0b101'.
what does bool do in python | python bool function | how do i use bool() in python => bool(x) turns a value into True or False. 0, empty strings, empty lists and None become False; almost everything else is True.
what does chr do in python | python chr function | how do i use chr() in python => chr(n) gives the character for a Unicode number, so chr(65) is 'A'. It is the opposite of ord.
what does dict do in python | python dict function | how do i use dict() in python => dict() makes a dictionary, like dict(name='Sam', age=12) or dict([('a', 1), ('b', 2)]).
what does dir do in python | python dir function | how do i use dir() in python => dir(obj) lists the names (attributes and methods) an object has, which is handy for exploring in the Python shell.
what does divmod do in python | python divmod function | how do i use divmod() in python => divmod(a, b) gives the whole-number quotient and the remainder together, so divmod(17, 5) is (3, 2).
what does enumerate do in python | python enumerate function | how do i use enumerate() in python => enumerate(items) gives the index and the item together in a loop: for i, name in enumerate(names): print(i, name). Use enumerate(items, 1) to start at 1.
what does eval do in python | python eval function | how do i use eval() in python => eval(text) runs a string as a Python expression and returns the result. Never use it on text a user typed, because it can run any code.
what does filter do in python | python filter function | how do i use filter() in python => filter(func, items) keeps only items where func returns True, like list(filter(lambda n: n > 0, nums)). A list comprehension often reads easier.
what does float do in python | python float function | how do i use float() in python => float(x) turns a number or a string like '3.5' into a decimal number. It raises ValueError if the text is not a number.
what does format do in python | python format function | how do i use format() in python => format(value, spec) formats a value, like format(3.14159, '.2f') giving '3.14' or format(1234567, ',') giving '1,234,567'.
what does getattr do in python | python getattr function | how do i use getattr() in python => getattr(obj, 'name', default) reads an attribute by its name as a string, and returns default instead of crashing if it is missing.
what does hasattr do in python | python hasattr function | how do i use hasattr() in python => hasattr(obj, 'name') is True if the object has that attribute or method.
what does hash do in python | python hash function | how do i use hash() in python => hash(x) gives the number Python uses to store x in sets and dict keys. Only immutable things like numbers, strings and tuples can be hashed.
what does help do in python | python help function | how do i use help() in python => help(thing) shows the built-in documentation for a function, module or class, like help(str.split), in the Python shell.
what does hex do in python | python hex function | how do i use hex() in python => hex(n) turns a whole number into a hexadecimal string, so hex(255) is '0xff'.
what does id do in python | python id function | how do i use id() in python => id(obj) gives a number that is unique for that object while it exists. Two names with the same id point to the same object.
what does input do in python | python input function | how do i use input() in python => input('prompt ') shows the prompt, waits for the user to type and press Enter, and returns what they typed as a string. Use int(input()) for numbers.
what does int do in python | python int function | how do i use int() in python => int(x) turns a string or number into a whole number. int('42') is 42 and int(3.9) is 3, because it cuts off the decimal instead of rounding.
what does isinstance do in python | python isinstance function | how do i use isinstance() in python => isinstance(x, int) is True if x is that type or a subclass of it. You can pass a tuple of types: isinstance(x, (int, float)).
what does issubclass do in python | python issubclass function | how do i use issubclass() in python => issubclass(Dog, Animal) is True if the Dog class inherits from Animal.
what does iter do in python | python iter function | how do i use iter() in python => iter(items) gets an iterator from a list or other iterable, which next() can step through one item at a time.
what does len do in python | python len function | how do i use len() in python => len(x) gives how many items are in a list, tuple, dict or set, or how many characters are in a string. len('hello') is 5.
python list function | how do i use list() in python => list(x) makes a new list from any iterable, like list('abc') giving ['a', 'b', 'c'] or list(range(3)) giving [0, 1, 2].
what does map do in python | python map function | how do i use map() in python => map(func, items) runs func on every item, like list(map(int, ['1', '2'])) giving [1, 2]. It returns a lazy map object, so wrap it in list() to see it.
what does max do in python | python max function | how do i use max() in python => max(items) gives the biggest item, and max(a, b, c) the biggest argument. max(words, key=len) gives the longest word.
what does min do in python | python min function | how do i use min() in python => min(items) gives the smallest item, and min(a, b) the smaller one. Use key= to compare by something, like min(people, key=lambda p: p.age).
what does next do in python | python next function | how do i use next() in python => next(iterator) gets the next item from an iterator, and next(it, default) returns default instead of raising StopIteration at the end.
what does oct do in python | python oct function | how do i use oct() in python => oct(n) turns a whole number into an octal (base 8) string, so oct(8) is '0o10'.
what does open do in python | python open function | how do i use open() in python => open(path, mode) opens a file. Use with open('notes.txt', 'r') as f: text = f.read(). Modes: 'r' read, 'w' write (erases first), 'a' append, 'b' for binary.
what does ord do in python | python ord function | how do i use ord() in python => ord(c) gives the Unicode number of one character, so ord('A') is 65. It is the opposite of chr.
what does pow do in python | python pow function | how do i use pow() in python => pow(a, b) is a to the power of b, the same as a ** b. pow(a, b, m) also takes the remainder by m quickly.
python print function | how do i use print() in python => print(a, b) shows values on screen separated by spaces. Use sep='' to change the separator and end='' to stop the new line at the end.
what does range do in python | python range function | how do i use range() in python => range(stop), range(start, stop) or range(start, stop, step) makes a sequence of whole numbers for loops. The stop number is not included, so range(5) is 0 to 4.
what does repr do in python | python repr function | how do i use repr() in python => repr(x) gives a string that shows the value the way a programmer would type it, like repr('hi') giving "'hi'" with quotes.
what does reversed do in python | python reversed function | how do i use reversed() in python => reversed(items) gives the items in reverse order as an iterator, like list(reversed([1, 2, 3])) giving [3, 2, 1]. It does not change the original.
what does round do in python | python round function | how do i use round() in python => round(x) rounds to the nearest whole number and round(x, 2) to 2 decimals. Halfway values round to the even number, so round(2.5) is 2 and round(3.5) is 4.
what does set do in python | python set function | how do i use set() in python => set(items) makes a set, which keeps only unique values with no order, like set([1, 1, 2]) giving {1, 2}. Use set() for an empty set, since {} is an empty dict.
what does setattr do in python | python setattr function | how do i use setattr() in python => setattr(obj, 'name', value) sets an attribute by its name as a string, the same as obj.name = value.
what does sorted do in python | python sorted function | how do i use sorted() in python => sorted(items) returns a new sorted list and leaves the original alone. Use reverse=True for big to small and key= to sort by something, like key=len.
what does str do in python | python str function | how do i use str() in python => str(x) turns a value into a string, like str(42) giving '42', so you can join it with other text.
what does sum do in python | python sum function | how do i use sum() in python => sum(numbers) adds up a list of numbers, like sum([1, 2, 3]) giving 6. sum(nums, 10) starts counting from 10.
what does super do in python | python super function | how do i use super() in python => super() lets a method call the same method in the parent class, most often super().__init__(...) inside a child class's __init__.
what does tuple do in python | python tuple function | how do i use tuple() in python => tuple(items) makes a tuple, an ordered list that cannot be changed, like tuple([1, 2]) giving (1, 2).
what does type do in python | python type function | how do i use type() in python => type(x) tells you the type of a value, like type(5) giving <class 'int'>. For checks, isinstance is usually better.
what does vars do in python | python vars function | how do i use vars() in python => vars(obj) returns the object's __dict__, a dictionary of its attributes, which is handy for printing what an object holds.
what does zip do in python | python zip function | how do i use zip() in python => zip(a, b) pairs up items from several lists: list(zip([1, 2], ['a', 'b'])) gives [(1, 'a'), (2, 'b')]. It stops at the shortest list.
what does callable do in python | python callable function | how do i use callable() in python => callable(x) is True if x can be called like a function, such as functions, classes and objects with __call__.
what does globals do in python | python globals function | how do i use globals() in python => globals() returns a dictionary of the module's global variables. You rarely need it in normal programs.
what does exec do in python | python exec function | how do i use exec() in python => exec(code) runs a string of Python statements. Like eval, never run text you did not write yourself.
what does frozenset do in python | python frozenset function | how do i use frozenset() in python => frozenset(items) is a set that cannot be changed after it is made, so it can be a dict key or go inside another set.
what does bytes do in python | python bytes function | how do i use bytes() in python => bytes makes an unchangeable sequence of bytes (numbers 0 to 255), like b'hi' or 'hi'.encode('utf-8'). Files opened with 'rb' give bytes.
what does bytearray do in python | python bytearray function | how do i use bytearray() in python => bytearray is like bytes but can be changed in place, which is useful for building binary data.
what does slice do in python | python slice function | how do i use slice() in python => slice(start, stop, step) makes a slice object, the same thing as writing items[start:stop:step].
what does complex do in python | python complex function | how do i use complex() in python => complex(real, imag) makes a complex number, like complex(2, 3) which is 2+3j. Python writes the imaginary unit as j.
what does object do in python | python object function | how do i use object() in python => object is the base class every Python class inherits from. object() makes a plain empty object, sometimes used as a unique marker.
what does property do in python | python property function | how do i use property() in python => property turns a method into an attribute you read without parentheses. Put @property above a method like def area(self) and read it as shape.area.
what does staticmethod do in python | python staticmethod function | how do i use staticmethod() in python => @staticmethod marks a method that does not get self or cls, so it works like a normal function stored in the class.
what does classmethod do in python | python classmethod function | how do i use classmethod() in python => @classmethod marks a method that gets the class as cls instead of an instance. It is often used for other ways to build objects, like Date.from_string().
what does breakpoint do in python | python breakpoint function | how do i use breakpoint() in python => breakpoint() pauses your program and opens the pdb debugger at that line, so you can look at variables and step through code.
what does ascii do in python | python ascii function | how do i use ascii() in python => ascii(x) is like repr(x) but turns non-ASCII characters into escape codes, so ascii('café') gives "'caf\xe9'".
what does aiter do in python | python aiter function | how do i use aiter() in python => aiter(x) gets an async iterator, the async version of iter(), used with async for loops.
what does memoryview do in python | python memoryview function | how do i use memoryview() in python => memoryview(data) lets you look at the bytes of an object like bytes or bytearray without copying them.
# tag: coding.python.strings
what does upper do to a string in python | python string upper method | how do i use .upper() on a string => s.upper() returns a copy with all letters in capitals, so 'hi'.upper() is 'HI'.
what does lower do to a string in python | python string lower method | how do i use .lower() on a string => s.lower() returns a copy in all lowercase, handy for comparing text without caring about capitals.
what does title do to a string in python | python string title method | how do i use .title() on a string => s.title() capitalizes the first letter of every word, so 'hello world'.title() is 'Hello World'.
what does capitalize do to a string in python | python string capitalize method | how do i use .capitalize() on a string => s.capitalize() makes the first character uppercase and the rest lowercase, so 'hELLO' becomes 'Hello'.
what does swapcase do to a string in python | python string swapcase method | how do i use .swapcase() on a string => s.swapcase() flips the case of every letter, so 'Hi' becomes 'hI'.
what does strip do to a string in python | python string strip method | how do i use .strip() on a string => s.strip() removes spaces, tabs and new lines from both ends. s.strip('!') removes that character from the ends instead.
what does lstrip do to a string in python | python string lstrip method | how do i use .lstrip() on a string => s.lstrip() removes whitespace (or the characters you give) only from the left side.
what does rstrip do to a string in python | python string rstrip method | how do i use .rstrip() on a string => s.rstrip() removes whitespace only from the right side, often used to drop the '\n' at the end of a line from a file.
what does split do to a string in python | python string split method | how do i use .split() on a string => s.split() breaks a string into a list of words on whitespace. s.split(',') splits on commas, so 'a,b'.split(',') is ['a', 'b'].
what does rsplit do to a string in python | python string rsplit method | how do i use .rsplit() on a string => s.rsplit(sep, maxsplit) splits from the right side, so 'a.b.c'.rsplit('.', 1) gives ['a.b', 'c'].
what does splitlines do to a string in python | python string splitlines method | how do i use .splitlines() on a string => s.splitlines() splits text into a list of lines and removes the line endings.
what does join do to a string in python | python string join method | how do i use .join() on a string => sep.join(items) glues a list of strings together with sep between them, so ', '.join(['a', 'b']) is 'a, b'. Every item must be a string.
what does replace do to a string in python | python string replace method | how do i use .replace() on a string => s.replace(old, new) returns a copy with every old part changed to new. Add a count to limit it: s.replace('a', 'b', 1).
python string find method | how do i use .find() on a string => s.find(sub) returns the index where sub first appears, or -1 if it is not there.
what does rfind do to a string in python | python string rfind method | how do i use .rfind() on a string => s.rfind(sub) returns the index of the last place sub appears, or -1.
what does index do to a string in python | python string index method | how do i use .index() on a string => s.index(sub) is like find but raises ValueError if sub is missing.
what does count do to a string in python | python string count method | how do i use .count() on a string => s.count(sub) counts how many times sub appears without overlapping, so 'banana'.count('a') is 3.
what does startswith do to a string in python | python string startswith method | how do i use .startswith() on a string => s.startswith(prefix) is True if the string begins with prefix. You can pass a tuple to check several.
what does endswith do to a string in python | python string endswith method | how do i use .endswith() on a string => s.endswith(suffix) is True if the string ends with suffix, like name.endswith('.png').
what does isdigit do to a string in python | python string isdigit method | how do i use .isdigit() on a string => s.isdigit() is True if the string is not empty and every character is a digit, so '123'.isdigit() is True but '-1' and '1.5' are False.
what does isalpha do to a string in python | python string isalpha method | how do i use .isalpha() on a string => s.isalpha() is True if the string is not empty and has only letters.
what does isalnum do to a string in python | python string isalnum method | how do i use .isalnum() on a string => s.isalnum() is True if every character is a letter or digit and the string is not empty.
what does isspace do to a string in python | python string isspace method | how do i use .isspace() on a string => s.isspace() is True if the string is not empty and has only whitespace.
what does isupper do to a string in python | python string isupper method | how do i use .isupper() on a string => s.isupper() is True if it has at least one letter and all its letters are uppercase.
what does islower do to a string in python | python string islower method | how do i use .islower() on a string => s.islower() is True if it has at least one letter and all its letters are lowercase.
what does isnumeric do to a string in python | python string isnumeric method | how do i use .isnumeric() on a string => s.isnumeric() is True for strings made of number characters, including things like '½' that isdigit rejects.
what does zfill do to a string in python | python string zfill method | how do i use .zfill() on a string => s.zfill(width) pads a number string with zeros on the left, so '7'.zfill(3) is '007'.
what does center do to a string in python | python string center method | how do i use .center() on a string => s.center(width) pads the string with spaces on both sides to that width. s.center(20, '*') uses stars.
what does ljust do to a string in python | python string ljust method | how do i use .ljust() on a string => s.ljust(width) pads on the right so text lines up in columns. rjust pads on the left.
what does rjust do to a string in python | python string rjust method | how do i use .rjust() on a string => s.rjust(width) pads on the left, good for lining up numbers on the right.
what does format do to a string in python | python string format method | how do i use .format() on a string => s.format(...) fills {} placeholders: 'Hi {}!'.format(name). f-strings like f'Hi {name}!' do the same and are easier to read.
what does encode do to a string in python | python string encode method | how do i use .encode() on a string => s.encode('utf-8') turns a string into bytes so it can be saved or sent. bytes.decode('utf-8') turns it back.
what does partition do to a string in python | python string partition method | how do i use .partition() on a string => s.partition(sep) splits at the first sep into a 3-part tuple: before, sep, after. 'key=value'.partition('=') gives ('key', '=', 'value').
what does removeprefix do to a string in python | python string removeprefix method | how do i use .removeprefix() on a string => s.removeprefix(prefix) removes that exact text from the start if it is there (Python 3.9 and newer).
what does removesuffix do to a string in python | python string removesuffix method | how do i use .removesuffix() on a string => s.removesuffix(suffix) removes that exact text from the end if it is there, like 'photo.png'.removesuffix('.png') (Python 3.9 and newer).
what does casefold do to a string in python | python string casefold method | how do i use .casefold() on a string => s.casefold() is a stronger lower() meant for comparing text without caring about case in every language.
what does expandtabs do to a string in python | python string expandtabs method | how do i use .expandtabs() on a string => s.expandtabs(4) replaces tab characters with spaces, using tab stops every 4 columns.
what does translate do to a string in python | python string translate method | how do i use .translate() on a string => s.translate(table) replaces or deletes characters using a table made with str.maketrans, like removing all punctuation at once.
# tag: coding.python.lists
what does list.append do in python | python list append method | how do i use .append() on a list => items.append(x) adds one item to the end of the list. It changes the list and returns None, so do not write items = items.append(x).
what does list.extend do in python | python list extend method | how do i use .extend() on a list => items.extend(other) adds every item from another list to the end. append(other) would add the whole list as one item instead.
what does list.insert do in python | python list insert method | how do i use .insert() on a list => items.insert(i, x) puts x at position i and shifts the rest right. items.insert(0, x) adds to the front.
what does list.remove do in python | python list remove method | how do i use .remove() on a list => items.remove(x) deletes the first item equal to x. It raises ValueError if x is not in the list.
what does list.pop do in python | python list pop method | how do i use .pop() on a list => items.pop() removes and returns the last item, and items.pop(i) removes the one at index i. It raises IndexError on an empty list.
what does list.clear do in python | python list clear method | how do i use .clear() on a list => items.clear() removes everything from the list, leaving it empty.
what does list.index do in python | python list index method | how do i use .index() on a list => items.index(x) returns the position of the first x. It raises ValueError if x is missing, so check with 'if x in items' first.
what does list.count do in python | python list count method | how do i use .count() on a list => items.count(x) returns how many times x appears in the list.
what does list.sort do in python | python list sort method | how do i use .sort() on a list => items.sort() sorts the list in place and returns None. Use items.sort(reverse=True) for big to small, or key=len to sort by length.
what does list.reverse do in python | python list reverse method | how do i use .reverse() on a list => items.reverse() flips the list in place. items[::-1] makes a reversed copy instead.
what does list.copy do in python | python list copy method | how do i use .copy() on a list => items.copy() makes a shallow copy, the same as items[:]. Lists inside it are still shared.
# tag: coding.python.dicts
what does dict.get do in python | python dictionary get method | how do i use .get() on a dictionary => d.get(key) returns the value or None if the key is missing, and d.get(key, 0) returns 0 instead. It never raises KeyError.
what does dict.keys do in python | python dictionary keys method | how do i use .keys() on a dictionary => d.keys() gives a live view of all the keys. Loop it with for k in d.keys(), or just for k in d.
what does dict.values do in python | python dictionary values method | how do i use .values() on a dictionary => d.values() gives a view of all the values, like sum(scores.values()) to add them up.
what does dict.items do in python | python dictionary items method | how do i use .items() on a dictionary => d.items() gives (key, value) pairs, so you can loop with for name, score in d.items().
what does dict.pop do in python | python dictionary pop method | how do i use .pop() on a dictionary => d.pop(key) removes the key and returns its value. d.pop(key, None) avoids a KeyError when it is missing.
what does dict.popitem do in python | python dictionary popitem method | how do i use .popitem() on a dictionary => d.popitem() removes and returns the last added (key, value) pair.
what does dict.update do in python | python dictionary update method | how do i use .update() on a dictionary => d.update(other) adds or overwrites keys from another dict. In Python 3.9+ you can also write d |= other.
what does dict.setdefault do in python | python dictionary setdefault method | how do i use .setdefault() on a dictionary => d.setdefault(key, default) returns the value if the key exists, otherwise sets it to default and returns that.
what does dict.clear do in python | python dictionary clear method | how do i use .clear() on a dictionary => d.clear() removes every key, leaving an empty dict.
what does dict.copy do in python | python dictionary copy method | how do i use .copy() on a dictionary => d.copy() makes a shallow copy of the dictionary.
what does dict.fromkeys do in python | python dictionary fromkeys method | how do i use .fromkeys() on a dictionary => dict.fromkeys(keys, value) makes a new dict with every key set to the same value, like dict.fromkeys(['a', 'b'], 0).
# tag: coding.python.sets
what does set.add do in python | python set add | how do i get the add of two sets => s.add(x) puts x in the set. Adding something already there does nothing.
what does set.discard do in python | python set discard | how do i get the discard of two sets => s.discard(x) removes x if it is there and does nothing if it is not.
what does set.union do in python | python set union | how do i get the union of two sets => a.union(b), or a | b, gives a new set with everything from both.
what does set.intersection do in python | python set intersection | how do i get the intersection of two sets => a.intersection(b), or a & b, gives the items that are in both sets.
what does set.difference do in python | python set difference | how do i get the difference of two sets => a.difference(b), or a - b, gives the items in a that are not in b.
what does set.symmetric_difference do in python | python set symmetric_difference | how do i get the symmetric difference of two sets => a.symmetric_difference(b), or a ^ b, gives items in one set or the other but not both.
what does set.issubset do in python | python set issubset | how do i get the issubset of two sets => a.issubset(b), or a <= b, is True if every item of a is also in b.
what does set.issuperset do in python | python set issuperset | how do i get the issuperset of two sets => a.issuperset(b), or a >= b, is True if a contains every item of b.
what does set.isdisjoint do in python | python set isdisjoint | how do i get the isdisjoint of two sets => a.isdisjoint(b) is True if the sets share no items.
what does set.remove do in python | remove vs discard python set => s.remove(x) deletes x from the set and raises KeyError if it is missing; use discard to avoid the error.
# tag: coding.python.stdlib
what does math.sqrt do in python | python math sqrt => math.sqrt(x) gives the square root, so math.sqrt(16) is 4.0. For a whole number answer use math.isqrt.
what does math.floor do in python | python math floor => math.floor(x) rounds down to a whole number, so math.floor(3.9) is 3 and math.floor(-1.5) is -2.
what does math.ceil do in python | python math ceil => math.ceil(x) rounds up to a whole number, so math.ceil(3.1) is 4.
what does math.trunc do in python | python math trunc | how do i use math.trunc => math.trunc(x) cuts off the decimal part, so math.trunc(-2.7) is -2.
what does math.pi do in python | python math pi | how do i use math.pi => math.pi is pi, about 3.141592653589793.
what does math.e do in python | python math e | how do i use math.e => math.e is Euler's number, about 2.718281828459045, the base of natural logarithms.
what does math.tau do in python | python math tau | how do i use math.tau => math.tau is 2 times pi, about 6.283, one full turn in radians.
what does math.inf do in python | python math inf | how do i use math.inf => math.inf is infinity, bigger than every number. -math.inf is smaller than every number.
what does math.pow do in python | python math pow => math.pow(x, y) is x to the power y and always returns a float. The ** operator keeps whole numbers whole.
what does math.sin do in python | python math sin => math.sin(x) is the sine of an angle in radians. Use math.radians(deg) to convert from degrees first.
what does math.cos do in python | python math cos => math.cos(x) is the cosine of an angle in radians.
what does math.tan do in python | python math tan => math.tan(x) is the tangent of an angle in radians.
what does math.atan2 do in python | python math atan2 => math.atan2(y, x) gives the angle in radians from the x axis to the point (x, y), handling every direction correctly.
what does math.radians do in python | python math radians | how do i use math.radians => math.radians(deg) converts degrees to radians, so math.radians(180) is pi.
what does math.degrees do in python | python math degrees | how do i use math.degrees => math.degrees(rad) converts radians to degrees.
what does math.log do in python | python math log => math.log(x) is the natural log, and math.log(x, base) uses another base, like math.log(8, 2) giving 3.0.
what does math.log10 do in python | python math log10 => math.log10(x) is the base 10 logarithm, so math.log10(1000) is 3.0.
what does math.log2 do in python | python math log2 | how do i use math.log2 => math.log2(x) is the base 2 logarithm, so math.log2(8) is 3.0.
what does math.exp do in python | python math exp => math.exp(x) is e to the power x.
what does math.factorial do in python | python math factorial | how do i use math.factorial => math.factorial(n) multiplies 1 x 2 x ... x n, so math.factorial(5) is 120.
what does math.gcd do in python | python math gcd | how do i use math.gcd => math.gcd(a, b) gives the greatest common divisor, the biggest number that divides both, so math.gcd(12, 18) is 6.
what does math.lcm do in python | python math lcm | how do i use math.lcm => math.lcm(a, b) gives the least common multiple, so math.lcm(4, 6) is 12 (Python 3.9+).
what does math.hypot do in python | python math hypot | how do i use math.hypot => math.hypot(x, y) gives the length of the hypotenuse, sqrt(x*x + y*y), handy for distances.
what does math.dist do in python | python math dist | how do i use math.dist => math.dist(p, q) gives the straight-line distance between two points, like math.dist((0, 0), (3, 4)) giving 5.0.
what does math.isclose do in python | python math isclose | how do i use math.isclose => math.isclose(a, b) checks if two floats are almost equal, which is the right way to compare decimals like 0.1 + 0.2 and 0.3.
what does math.fabs do in python | python math fabs | how do i use math.fabs => math.fabs(x) gives the absolute value as a float.
what does math.comb do in python | python math comb | how do i use math.comb => math.comb(n, k) counts the ways to choose k items from n without caring about order, so math.comb(5, 2) is 10.
what does math.perm do in python | python math perm | how do i use math.perm => math.perm(n, k) counts the ways to arrange k items out of n where order matters.
what does math.isqrt do in python | python math isqrt | how do i use math.isqrt => math.isqrt(n) gives the whole-number square root rounded down, so math.isqrt(10) is 3.
what does math.prod do in python | python math prod | how do i use math.prod => math.prod(items) multiplies all the numbers together, like math.prod([2, 3, 4]) giving 24.
what does math.fsum do in python | python math fsum | how do i use math.fsum => math.fsum(items) adds floats with less rounding error than sum().
what does math.copysign do in python | python math copysign | how do i use math.copysign => math.copysign(x, y) gives x with the sign of y.
what does math.isnan do in python | python math isnan => math.isnan(x) is True if x is NaN (not a number), which you get from things like float('nan').
what does random.random do in python | python random random | how do i use random.random => random.random() gives a random float from 0.0 up to but not including 1.0.
what does random.randint do in python | python random randint | how do i use random.randint => random.randint(a, b) gives a random whole number from a to b, including both ends, so randint(1, 6) is a dice roll.
what does random.randrange do in python | python random randrange | how do i use random.randrange => random.randrange(start, stop, step) picks a random number from range(start, stop, step); stop is not included.
what does random.choice do in python | python random choice | how do i use random.choice => random.choice(items) picks one random item from a list or string.
what does random.choices do in python | how do i use random.choices => random.choices(items, k=3) picks 3 items with replacement (repeats allowed). Add weights=[...] to make some more likely.
what does random.sample do in python | python random sample | how do i use random.sample => random.sample(items, k) picks k different items with no repeats, like drawing cards.
what does random.shuffle do in python | python random shuffle | how do i use random.shuffle => random.shuffle(items) mixes a list into random order in place and returns None.
what does random.uniform do in python | python random uniform | how do i use random.uniform => random.uniform(a, b) gives a random float between a and b.
what does random.seed do in python | python random seed | how do i use random.seed => random.seed(n) sets the starting point so you get the same random numbers every run, which helps with testing.
what does random.gauss do in python | python random gauss | how do i use random.gauss => random.gauss(mu, sigma) gives a random number from a bell curve with that average and spread.
what does os.getcwd do in python | python os getcwd | how do i use os.getcwd => os.getcwd() returns the working directory, the folder your program is running from.
what does os.chdir do in python | python os chdir | how do i use os.chdir => os.chdir(path) changes the working directory to that folder.
what does os.listdir do in python | python os listdir | how do i use os.listdir => os.listdir(path) returns a list of the names of files and folders inside a folder.
what does os.mkdir do in python | python os mkdir | how do i use os.mkdir => os.mkdir(path) makes one new folder and raises FileExistsError if it is already there.
what does os.makedirs do in python | python os makedirs | how do i use os.makedirs => os.makedirs(path, exist_ok=True) makes a folder and any missing parent folders, without an error if it exists.
what does os.remove do in python | python os remove | how do i use os.remove => os.remove(path) deletes a file. It cannot delete folders; use os.rmdir or shutil.rmtree.
what does os.rmdir do in python | python os rmdir | how do i use os.rmdir => os.rmdir(path) deletes an empty folder.
what does os.rename do in python | python os rename | how do i use os.rename => os.rename(old, new) renames or moves a file or folder.
what does os.walk do in python | python os walk | how do i use os.walk => os.walk(top) goes through a folder and all its subfolders, giving (folder, subfolders, files) for each, so you can process every file.
what does os.getenv do in python | python os getenv | how do i use os.getenv => os.getenv('NAME', default) reads an environment variable, or returns default if it is not set.
what does os.environ do in python | python os environ | how do i use os.environ => os.environ is a dict-like object of environment variables, like os.environ['PATH'].
what does os.system do in python | python os system | how do i use os.system => os.system('command') runs a shell command. subprocess.run is the more modern and safer choice.
what does os.sep do in python | python os sep | how do i use os.sep => os.sep is the folder separator for the computer: a backslash on Windows and '/' on macOS and Linux.
what does os.cpu_count do in python | python os cpu count | how do i use os.cpu_count => os.cpu_count() returns how many CPU cores (logical processors) the computer has.
what does os.scandir do in python | python os scandir | how do i use os.scandir => os.scandir(path) lists folder entries with extra info like is_file() and stat(), and is faster than listdir when you need that info.
what does os.path.join do in python | python os.path join | how do i use os.path.join => os.path.join('folder', 'file.txt') builds a path with the right separator for the computer.
what does os.path.exists do in python | python os.path exists | how do i use os.path.exists => os.path.exists(path) is True if a file or folder is at that path.
what does os.path.isfile do in python | python os.path isfile | how do i use os.path.isfile => os.path.isfile(path) is True if the path is an existing file.
what does os.path.isdir do in python | python os.path isdir | how do i use os.path.isdir => os.path.isdir(path) is True if the path is an existing folder.
what does os.path.basename do in python | python os.path basename | how do i use os.path.basename => os.path.basename('/a/b/photo.png') gives 'photo.png', the last part of a path.
what does os.path.dirname do in python | python os.path dirname | how do i use os.path.dirname => os.path.dirname('/a/b/photo.png') gives '/a/b', the folder part of a path.
what does os.path.splitext do in python | python os.path splitext | how do i use os.path.splitext => os.path.splitext('photo.png') gives ('photo', '.png'), splitting off the file extension.
what does os.path.abspath do in python | python os.path abspath | how do i use os.path.abspath => os.path.abspath(path) turns a relative path into a full path from the root.
what does os.path.getsize do in python | python os.path getsize | how do i use os.path.getsize => os.path.getsize(path) returns a file's size in bytes.
what does os.path.expanduser do in python | python os.path expanduser | how do i use os.path.expanduser => os.path.expanduser('~/notes') replaces ~ with the user's home folder.
what does sys.argv do in python | python sys argv | how do i use sys.argv => sys.argv is the list of command-line arguments; sys.argv[0] is the script name and the rest are what was typed after it.
what does sys.exit do in python | python sys exit | how do i use sys.exit => sys.exit() stops the program. sys.exit(1) signals an error to whatever started it.
what does sys.path do in python | python sys path | how do i use sys.path => sys.path is the list of folders Python searches when you import a module.
what does sys.version do in python | python sys version | how do i use sys.version => sys.version is a string describing the Python version that is running.
what does sys.platform do in python | python sys platform | how do i use sys.platform => sys.platform tells you the operating system, like 'win32', 'darwin' (macOS) or 'linux'.
what does sys.stdin do in python | python sys stdin | how do i use sys.stdin => sys.stdin is the input stream; sys.stdin.readline() reads a line, often faster than input() in big programs.
what does sys.getrecursionlimit do in python | python sys getrecursionlimit | how do i use sys.getrecursionlimit => sys.getrecursionlimit() shows how deep recursion can go before RecursionError, usually 1000. sys.setrecursionlimit changes it.
what does sys.executable do in python | python sys executable | how do i use sys.executable => sys.executable is the full path to the Python program that is running your script.
what does time.time do in python | python time time | how do i use time.time => time.time() returns the seconds since January 1, 1970 as a float. Subtract two of them to measure how long something took.
what does time.sleep do in python | python time sleep | how do i use time.sleep => time.sleep(seconds) pauses the program, like time.sleep(0.5) for half a second.
what does time.perf_counter do in python | python time perf counter | how do i use time.perf_counter => time.perf_counter() is a very precise clock for measuring how long code takes; subtract a start value from an end value.
what does time.strftime do in python | python time strftime | how do i use time.strftime => time.strftime('%H:%M:%S') formats the local time as text using codes like %Y year, %m month, %d day.
what does time.localtime do in python | python time localtime | how do i use time.localtime => time.localtime() returns the local date and time as a struct with fields like tm_year and tm_hour.
what does time.monotonic do in python | python time monotonic | how do i use time.monotonic => time.monotonic() is a clock that never goes backward, good for timeouts.
what does datetime.datetime do in python | python datetime datetime | how do i use datetime.datetime => datetime.datetime holds a date and a time together. datetime.datetime.now() gives the local date and time.
what does datetime.date do in python | python datetime date | how do i use datetime.date => datetime.date holds just a date. datetime.date.today() gives today's date, and date(2025, 12, 25) makes one.
what does datetime.timedelta do in python | python datetime timedelta | how do i use datetime.timedelta => datetime.timedelta is a length of time, like timedelta(days=7). Add it to a date to move forward, or subtract two dates to get one.
what does datetime.time do in python | python datetime time | how do i use datetime.time => datetime.time holds a time of day without a date, like time(14, 30).
what does datetime.timezone do in python | python datetime timezone | how do i use datetime.timezone => datetime.timezone represents a fixed UTC offset; datetime.now(timezone.utc) gives an aware UTC time.
what does json.dumps do in python | python json dumps | how do i use json.dumps => json.dumps(obj) turns a Python dict or list into a JSON string. Add indent=2 to make it easy to read.
what does json.loads do in python | python json loads | how do i use json.loads => json.loads(text) turns a JSON string into Python dicts and lists.
what does json.dump do in python | how do i use json.dump => json.dump(obj, f) writes JSON straight into an open file.
what does json.load do in python | how do i use json.load => json.load(f) reads JSON from an open file into Python objects.
what does re.search do in python | python re search | how do i use re.search => re.search(pattern, text) finds the first match anywhere in the text and returns a Match object or None.
what does re.match do in python | python re match | how do i use re.match => re.match(pattern, text) only matches at the start of the text. Use re.search to look anywhere.
what does re.fullmatch do in python | python re fullmatch | how do i use re.fullmatch => re.fullmatch(pattern, text) only succeeds if the whole string matches, good for checking input formats.
what does re.findall do in python | python re findall | how do i use re.findall => re.findall(pattern, text) returns a list of every match, like re.findall(r'\d+', 'a1b22') giving ['1', '22'].
what does re.sub do in python | python re sub | how do i use re.sub => re.sub(pattern, replacement, text) replaces every match, like re.sub(r'\s+', ' ', text) to squash extra spaces.
what does re.split do in python | python re split | how do i use re.split => re.split(pattern, text) splits text wherever the pattern matches, like splitting on commas or spaces at once.
what does re.compile do in python | python re compile | how do i use re.compile => re.compile(pattern) saves a pattern as an object you can reuse, with methods like .search and .findall.
what does re.finditer do in python | python re finditer | how do i use re.finditer => re.finditer(pattern, text) loops over Match objects, so you get each match's position too.
what does re.ignorecase do in python | python re ignorecase | how do i use re.ignorecase => re.IGNORECASE (or re.I) is a flag that makes a pattern ignore uppercase and lowercase differences.
what does collections.counter do in python | python collections counter | how do i use collections.counter => collections.Counter(items) counts how many times each item appears, like Counter('hello')['l'] being 2. .most_common(3) gives the top 3.
what does collections.defaultdict do in python | python collections defaultdict | how do i use collections.defaultdict => collections.defaultdict(list) is a dict that makes a default value for missing keys, so d[k].append(x) works without checking first.
what does collections.deque do in python | python collections deque | how do i use collections.deque => collections.deque is a list-like queue that adds and removes from both ends fast, with append, appendleft, pop and popleft.
what does collections.namedtuple do in python | python collections namedtuple | how do i use collections.namedtuple => collections.namedtuple('Point', ['x', 'y']) makes a small tuple class whose items have names, so you can write p.x.
what does collections.ordereddict do in python | python collections ordereddict | how do i use collections.ordereddict => collections.OrderedDict is a dict with extra ordering methods like move_to_end. Normal dicts keep insertion order since Python 3.7.
what does collections.chainmap do in python | python collections chainmap | how do i use collections.chainmap => collections.ChainMap groups several dicts so lookups check each one in order, like settings overriding defaults.
what does itertools.count do in python | python itertools count | how do i use itertools.count => itertools.count(start, step) counts up forever, like an endless range.
what does itertools.cycle do in python | python itertools cycle | how do i use itertools.cycle => itertools.cycle(items) repeats the items over and over forever.
what does itertools.repeat do in python | python itertools repeat | how do i use itertools.repeat => itertools.repeat(x, n) gives the same value n times (or forever without n).
what does itertools.chain do in python | python itertools chain | how do i use itertools.chain => itertools.chain(a, b) loops through several lists one after another as if they were one.
what does itertools.permutations do in python | python itertools permutations | how do i use itertools.permutations => itertools.permutations(items, r) gives every ordering of r items, so permutations('abc', 2) includes ('a', 'b') and ('b', 'a').
what does itertools.combinations do in python | python itertools combinations | how do i use itertools.combinations => itertools.combinations(items, r) gives every group of r items where order does not matter.
what does itertools.product do in python | python itertools product | how do i use itertools.product => itertools.product(a, b) gives every pair from both lists, like nested for loops. product('ab', repeat=2) gives aa, ab, ba, bb.
what does itertools.groupby do in python | python itertools groupby | how do i use itertools.groupby => itertools.groupby(items, key) groups items that are next to each other with the same key, so sort by that key first.
what does itertools.accumulate do in python | python itertools accumulate | how do i use itertools.accumulate => itertools.accumulate(nums) gives running totals, so [1, 2, 3] becomes 1, 3, 6.
what does itertools.islice do in python | python itertools islice | how do i use itertools.islice => itertools.islice(it, n) takes the first n items from any iterator, like slicing but for things without indexes.
what does itertools.zip_longest do in python | python itertools zip longest | how do i use itertools.zip_longest => itertools.zip_longest(a, b, fillvalue=None) zips lists of different lengths and fills the gaps.
what does itertools.pairwise do in python | python itertools pairwise | how do i use itertools.pairwise => itertools.pairwise(items) gives each item with the next one, like (1, 2), (2, 3) (Python 3.10+).
what does functools.lru_cache do in python | python functools lru cache | how do i use functools.lru_cache => @functools.lru_cache remembers results of a function for arguments it has seen, which makes slow recursive functions like Fibonacci very fast.
what does functools.cache do in python | python functools cache | how do i use functools.cache => @functools.cache is a simpler unlimited version of lru_cache that remembers every result (Python 3.9+).
what does functools.reduce do in python | python functools reduce | how do i use functools.reduce => functools.reduce(func, items) combines items into one value step by step, like reduce(lambda a, b: a * b, [1, 2, 3, 4]) giving 24.
what does functools.partial do in python | python functools partial | how do i use functools.partial => functools.partial(func, x) makes a new function with some arguments already filled in.
what does functools.wraps do in python | python functools wraps | how do i use functools.wraps => @functools.wraps(func) is used inside decorators so the wrapped function keeps its original name and docstring.
what does pathlib.path do in python | python pathlib path | how do i use pathlib.path => pathlib.Path(path) makes a path object with handy tools: p.exists(), p.read_text(), p / 'file.txt', p.suffix, p.name and p.iterdir().
what does shutil.copy do in python | python shutil copy | how do i use shutil.copy => shutil.copy(src, dst) copies a file. shutil.copy2 also keeps the file's timestamps.
what does shutil.copytree do in python | python shutil copytree | how do i use shutil.copytree => shutil.copytree(src, dst) copies a whole folder and everything inside it.
what does shutil.rmtree do in python | python shutil rmtree | how do i use shutil.rmtree => shutil.rmtree(path) deletes a folder and everything in it. Be careful, it does not go to the recycle bin.
what does shutil.move do in python | python shutil move | how do i use shutil.move => shutil.move(src, dst) moves a file or folder, even to another drive.
what does shutil.make_archive do in python | python shutil make archive | how do i use shutil.make_archive => shutil.make_archive('backup', 'zip', folder) zips a whole folder into backup.zip.
what does shutil.which do in python | python shutil which | how do i use shutil.which => shutil.which('git') returns the full path of a program on the PATH, or None if it is not installed.
what does shutil.disk_usage do in python | python shutil disk usage | how do i use shutil.disk_usage => shutil.disk_usage(path) returns the total, used and free space of that drive in bytes.
what does subprocess.run do in python | python subprocess run | how do i use subprocess.run => subprocess.run(['git', 'status'], capture_output=True, text=True) runs another program and waits; the result's .stdout holds its output and .returncode its exit code.
what does subprocess.popen do in python | python subprocess popen | how do i use subprocess.popen => subprocess.Popen starts another program without waiting, so you can talk to it or keep working while it runs.
what does subprocess.check_output do in python | python subprocess check output | how do i use subprocess.check_output => subprocess.check_output(cmd) runs a command and returns its output, raising an error if it fails.
what does statistics.mean do in python | python statistics mean | how do i use statistics.mean => statistics.mean(nums) gives the average.
what does statistics.median do in python | python statistics median | how do i use statistics.median => statistics.median(nums) gives the middle value after sorting.
what does statistics.mode do in python | python statistics mode | how do i use statistics.mode => statistics.mode(items) gives the most common value.
what does statistics.stdev do in python | python statistics stdev | how do i use statistics.stdev => statistics.stdev(nums) gives the sample standard deviation, how spread out the numbers are.
what does string.ascii_letters do in python | python string ascii letters | how do i use string.ascii_letters => string.ascii_letters is 'abc...zABC...Z', all English letters in one string.
what does string.ascii_lowercase do in python | python string ascii lowercase | how do i use string.ascii_lowercase => string.ascii_lowercase is 'abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz'.
what does string.digits do in python | python string digits | how do i use string.digits => string.digits is '0123456789'.
what does string.punctuation do in python | python string punctuation | how do i use string.punctuation => string.punctuation is a string of ASCII punctuation marks like !"#$%&'()*+,-./ and more.
what does string.ascii_uppercase do in python | python string ascii uppercase | how do i use string.ascii_uppercase => string.ascii_uppercase is 'ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ'.
what does csv.reader do in python | python csv reader | how do i use csv.reader => csv.reader(f) reads a CSV file row by row, giving each row as a list of strings. Open the file with newline=''.
what does csv.writer do in python | python csv writer | how do i use csv.writer => csv.writer(f) writes rows to a CSV file with writer.writerow([...]).
what does csv.dictreader do in python | python csv dictreader | how do i use csv.dictreader => csv.DictReader(f) reads each row as a dict using the header row as keys.
what does csv.dictwriter do in python | python csv dictwriter | how do i use csv.dictwriter => csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=[...]) writes dicts as rows; call writeheader() first.
what does copy.copy do in python | python copy copy | how do i use copy.copy => copy.copy(x) makes a shallow copy: a new outer object, but things inside are shared.
what does copy.deepcopy do in python | python copy deepcopy | how do i use copy.deepcopy => copy.deepcopy(x) copies an object and everything inside it, so changing the copy never affects the original.
what does turtle.forward do | python turtle forward | how do i use forward in turtle => turtle.forward(100) moves the turtle 100 steps the way it faces, drawing a line if the pen is down.
what does turtle.backward do | python turtle backward | how do i use backward in turtle => turtle.backward(50) moves the turtle back without turning around.
what does turtle.left do | python turtle left | how do i use left in turtle => turtle.left(90) turns the turtle left by 90 degrees.
what does turtle.right do | python turtle right | how do i use right in turtle => turtle.right(90) turns the turtle right by 90 degrees.
what does turtle.penup do | python turtle penup | how do i use penup in turtle => turtle.penup() lifts the pen so moving does not draw. pendown() puts it back.
what does turtle.pendown do | python turtle pendown | how do i use pendown in turtle => turtle.pendown() puts the pen down so moving draws again.
what does turtle.color do | python turtle color | how do i use color in turtle => turtle.color('red') sets the pen and fill color. turtle.color('red', 'yellow') sets them separately.
what does turtle.goto do | python turtle goto | how do i use goto in turtle => turtle.goto(x, y) moves the turtle straight to that point; (0, 0) is the middle of the window.
what does turtle.circle do | python turtle circle | how do i use circle in turtle => turtle.circle(50) draws a circle with radius 50. circle(50, 180) draws half a circle.
what does turtle.begin_fill do | python turtle begin fill | how do i use begin_fill in turtle => Call turtle.begin_fill() before drawing a shape and turtle.end_fill() after to fill it with the fill color.
what does turtle.speed do | python turtle speed | how do i use speed in turtle => turtle.speed(0) makes drawing as fast as possible; 1 is slowest and 10 is fast.
what does turtle.done do | python turtle done | how do i use done in turtle => turtle.done() keeps the window open after drawing, so it does not close right away.
what does turtle.bgcolor do | python turtle bgcolor | how do i use bgcolor in turtle => turtle.bgcolor('black') sets the window's background color.
what does turtle.pensize do | python turtle pensize | how do i use pensize in turtle => turtle.pensize(5) makes the drawn lines 5 pixels thick.
what does turtle.hideturtle do | python turtle hideturtle | how do i use hideturtle in turtle => turtle.hideturtle() hides the arrow so only your drawing shows.
what does turtle.write do | python turtle write | how do i use write in turtle => turtle.write('Hi', font=('Arial', 16, 'normal')) writes text where the turtle is.
what does glob.glob do in python | how do i use glob.glob => glob.glob('*.txt') returns a list of file paths matching a pattern. Use '**/*.txt' with recursive=True to search subfolders.
what does zipfile.zipfile do in python | python zipfile zipfile | how do i use zipfile.zipfile => zipfile.ZipFile('a.zip') opens a zip file; use .extractall(folder) to unzip or open it with 'w' and .write(path) to add files.
what does hashlib.sha256 do in python | python hashlib sha256 | how do i use hashlib.sha256 => hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest() gives the SHA-256 fingerprint of some bytes, used to check files are the same or unchanged.
what does hashlib.md5 do in python | python hashlib md5 | how do i use hashlib.md5 => hashlib.md5(data).hexdigest() gives an MD5 hash. It is fine for spotting changed files but not safe for passwords or security.
what does uuid.uuid4 do in python | python uuid uuid4 | how do i use uuid.uuid4 => uuid.uuid4() makes a random unique ID like 'f47ac10b-58cc-...', handy for naming things that must never clash.
what does secrets.token_hex do in python | python secrets token hex | how do i use secrets.token_hex => secrets.token_hex(16) makes a random, secure hex string, good for tokens and keys.
what does secrets.choice do in python | python secrets choice | how do i use secrets.choice => secrets.choice(items) picks a random item in a way that is safe for passwords and codes, unlike random.choice.
what does secrets.randbelow do in python | python secrets randbelow | how do i use secrets.randbelow => secrets.randbelow(n) gives a secure random whole number from 0 up to n - 1.
what does base64.b64encode do in python | python base64 b64encode | how do i use base64.b64encode => base64.b64encode(data) turns bytes into Base64 text-safe bytes, used to send images or files inside JSON or email. b64decode turns it back.
what does base64.b64decode do in python | python base64 b64decode | how do i use base64.b64decode => base64.b64decode(text) turns Base64 text back into the original bytes.
what does textwrap.wrap do in python | python textwrap wrap | how do i use textwrap.wrap => textwrap.wrap(text, width=40) splits long text into a list of lines no longer than 40 characters.
what does textwrap.dedent do in python | python textwrap dedent | how do i use textwrap.dedent => textwrap.dedent(text) removes the common indentation from every line, handy for triple-quoted strings inside functions.
what does calendar.month do in python | python calendar month | how do i use calendar.month => calendar.month(2025, 6) returns a text calendar of that month you can print.
what does calendar.isleap do in python | python calendar isleap | how do i use calendar.isleap => calendar.isleap(year) is True if that year is a leap year.
what does platform.system do in python | python platform system | how do i use platform.system => platform.system() returns 'Windows', 'Darwin' (macOS) or 'Linux'.
what does platform.python_version do in python | python platform python version | how do i use platform.python_version => platform.python_version() returns the Python version as a string like '3.12.4'.
what does webbrowser.open do in python | python webbrowser open | how do i use webbrowser.open => webbrowser.open(url) opens a web page in the default browser.
what does timeit.timeit do in python | python timeit timeit | how do i use timeit.timeit => timeit.timeit('code', number=1000) runs a small piece of code many times and returns the total seconds, for comparing which version is faster.
what does getpass.getpass do in python | python getpass getpass | how do i use getpass.getpass => getpass.getpass('Password: ') reads typed text without showing it on screen.
what does sqlite3.connect do in python | python sqlite3 connect | how do i use sqlite3.connect => sqlite3.connect('game.db') opens (or creates) a small database file. Use conn.execute with SQL and ? placeholders, then conn.commit() to save changes.
what does sqlite3.row do in python | python sqlite3 row | how do i use sqlite3.row => Setting conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row lets you read query results by column name, like row['name'].
what does threading.thread do in python | how do i use threading.thread => threading.Thread(target=func).start() runs func in a background thread; .join() waits for it to finish.
what does threading.lock do in python | python threading lock | how do i use threading.lock => threading.Lock() stops two threads from changing the same data at once; use it with `with lock:`.
what does queue.queue do in python | python queue queue | how do i use queue.queue => queue.Queue() is a thread-safe first-in first-out queue with put() and get(), perfect for passing work between threads.
what does heapq.heappush do in python | python heapq heappush | how do i use heapq.heappush => heapq.heappush(heap, x) adds x to a list kept as a min-heap, so the smallest item is always at heap[0].
what does heapq.heappop do in python | python heapq heappop | how do i use heapq.heappop => heapq.heappop(heap) removes and returns the smallest item from a heap list.
what does heapq.nlargest do in python | python heapq nlargest | how do i use heapq.nlargest => heapq.nlargest(3, items) returns the 3 biggest items without sorting everything. nsmallest does the opposite.
what does bisect.bisect_left do in python | python bisect bisect left | how do i use bisect.bisect_left => bisect.bisect_left(sorted_list, x) finds where x would go in a sorted list using binary search.
what does bisect.insort do in python | python bisect insort | how do i use bisect.insort => bisect.insort(sorted_list, x) puts x into a sorted list at the right spot so it stays sorted.
what does operator.itemgetter do in python | python operator itemgetter | how do i use operator.itemgetter => operator.itemgetter('score') makes a function that pulls that key, handy as a sort key: sorted(rows, key=itemgetter('score')).
what does operator.attrgetter do in python | python operator attrgetter | how do i use operator.attrgetter => operator.attrgetter('age') makes a function that reads an attribute, useful as a sort key for objects.
what does contextlib.suppress do in python | python contextlib suppress | how do i use contextlib.suppress => contextlib.suppress(FileNotFoundError) used in a with block ignores that error, a short way to try something that may fail.
what does contextlib.contextmanager do in python | python contextlib contextmanager | how do i use contextlib.contextmanager => @contextlib.contextmanager turns a generator function into a context manager: code before yield runs on enter and after yield on exit.
what does tempfile.temporarydirectory do in python | python tempfile temporarydirectory | how do i use tempfile.temporarydirectory => tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() makes a temporary folder that is deleted when the with block ends.
what does tempfile.namedtemporaryfile do in python | python tempfile namedtemporaryfile | how do i use tempfile.namedtemporaryfile => tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile() makes a temporary file with a real path that is removed when closed (by default).
what does fractions.fraction do in python | python fractions fraction | how do i use fractions.fraction => fractions.Fraction(1, 3) stores exact fractions, so Fraction(1, 3) + Fraction(1, 6) gives Fraction(1, 2) with no rounding.
what does decimal.decimal do in python | python decimal decimal | how do i use decimal.decimal => decimal.Decimal('0.1') stores decimals exactly, so Decimal('0.1') + Decimal('0.2') equals Decimal('0.3'). Pass strings, not floats.
what does socket.socket do in python | python socket socket | how do i use socket.socket => socket.socket() makes a network connection endpoint for low-level networking; most programs use requests or http libraries instead.
what does socket.gethostname do in python | python socket gethostname | how do i use socket.gethostname => socket.gethostname() returns the computer's network name.
what does unittest.testcase do in python | python unittest testcase | how do i use unittest.testcase => unittest.TestCase is the base class for tests: write methods starting with test_ that use self.assertEqual and run with python -m unittest.
what does dataclasses.dataclass do in python | how do i use dataclasses.dataclass => @dataclasses.dataclass writes __init__, __repr__ and __eq__ for a class from its annotated fields.
what does dataclasses.field do in python | python dataclasses field | how do i use dataclasses.field => dataclasses.field(default_factory=list) gives each object its own new list as a default, avoiding the shared default problem.
what does dataclasses.asdict do in python | python dataclasses asdict | how do i use dataclasses.asdict => dataclasses.asdict(obj) turns a dataclass object into a dictionary, handy before saving it as JSON.
what does enum.enum do in python | how do i use enum.enum => enum.Enum is the base class for named constants: class Color(Enum): RED = 1. Use Color.RED, and Color.RED.name gives 'RED'.
what does enum.auto do in python | python enum auto | how do i use enum.auto => enum.auto() fills in enum values for you so you do not have to number them.
what does typing.optional do in python | python typing optional | how do i use typing.optional => typing.Optional[int] means an int or None. In Python 3.10+ you can write int | None instead.
what does typing.any do in python | python typing any | how do i use typing.any => typing.Any means any type at all, which turns off type checking for that value.
what does typing.callable do in python | python typing callable | how do i use typing.callable => typing.Callable[[int], str] is the type of a function that takes an int and returns a str.
what does urllib.request.urlopen do in python | python urllib.request urlopen | how do i use urllib.request.urlopen => urllib.request.urlopen(url) downloads a web page with only the standard library; .read() gives the bytes. The requests package is easier.
what does urllib.parse.urlencode do in python | python urllib.parse urlencode | how do i use urllib.parse.urlencode => urllib.parse.urlencode({'q': 'cats'}) builds a safe query string like 'q=cats' for URLs.
what does urllib.parse.quote do in python | python urllib.parse quote | how do i use urllib.parse.quote => urllib.parse.quote('a b') makes text safe for a URL, giving 'a%20b'.
what does string.template do in python | python string template | how do i use string.template => string.Template('Hi $name').substitute(name='Sam') fills in $ placeholders, a simple way to make text from user templates.
what does logging.basicconfig do in python | python logging basicconfig | how do i use logging.basicconfig => logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO) sets up logging to show INFO messages and above, with an optional filename= to log to a file.
what does logging.getlogger do in python | python logging getlogger | how do i use logging.getlogger => logging.getLogger(__name__) gets a named logger for your module, so messages show where they came from.
what does argparse.argumentparser do in python | python argparse argumentparser | how do i use argparse.argumentparser => argparse.ArgumentParser() reads command-line options: add_argument('--count', type=int) then parse_args() gives args.count.
what does configparser.configparser do in python | python configparser configparser | how do i use configparser.configparser => configparser.ConfigParser() reads and writes .ini settings files with [sections] and key = value lines.
what does pprint.pprint do in python | python pprint pprint | how do i use pprint.pprint => pprint.pprint(data) prints big nested dicts and lists neatly over several lines.
what does shlex.split do in python | python shlex split | how do i use shlex.split => shlex.split('cmd "two words"') splits a command line the way a shell would, keeping quoted parts together.
what does difflib.get_close_matches do in python | python difflib get close matches | how do i use difflib.get_close_matches => difflib.get_close_matches(word, options) finds the most similar strings, great for 'did you mean' suggestions.
what does struct.pack do in python | python struct pack | how do i use struct.pack => struct.pack('<hf', 1, 2.5) packs numbers into bytes in an exact layout, useful for files or talking to hardware.
what does struct.unpack do in python | python struct unpack | how do i use struct.unpack => struct.unpack('<hf', data) reads numbers back out of bytes using the same format string.
what does array.array do in python | python array array | how do i use array.array => array.array('i', [1, 2, 3]) stores numbers of one type compactly, using less memory than a list.
what does atexit.register do in python | python atexit register | how do i use atexit.register => atexit.register(func) runs func when the program exits normally, good for saving or cleanup.
what does signal.signal do in python | python signal signal | how do i use signal.signal => signal.signal(signal.SIGINT, handler) lets you run your own function when the program gets a signal like Ctrl+C.
what does http.server.httpserver do in python | python http.server httpserver | how do i use http.server.httpserver => http.server.HTTPServer is a basic web server class. From a terminal, python -m http.server 8000 serves the files in a folder at localhost:8000.
what does tkinter.tk do in python | python tkinter tk | how do i use tkinter.tk => tkinter.Tk() makes the main window. Add widgets to it and call root.mainloop() to show it and react to clicks.
what does tkinter.label do in python | python tkinter label | how do i use tkinter.label => tkinter.Label(root, text='Hi') shows text or an image in a tkinter window. Call .pack() or .grid() to place it.
what does tkinter.button do in python | python tkinter button | how do i use tkinter.button => tkinter.Button(root, text='Go', command=func) makes a button that calls func when clicked.
what does tkinter.entry do in python | python tkinter entry | how do i use tkinter.entry => tkinter.Entry(root) is a one-line text box; read what was typed with entry.get().
what does tkinter.canvas do in python | python tkinter canvas | how do i use tkinter.canvas => tkinter.Canvas(root, width=400, height=300) is a drawing area with create_line, create_rectangle, create_oval and create_text.
what does tkinter.frame do in python | python tkinter frame | how do i use tkinter.frame => tkinter.Frame(root) is a container for grouping widgets, so you can lay out sections of a window.
what does tkinter.messagebox do in python | python tkinter messagebox | how do i use tkinter.messagebox => tkinter.messagebox.showinfo('Title', 'Text') pops up a message box. There are also showerror and askyesno.
what does tkinter.stringvar do in python | python tkinter stringvar | how do i use tkinter.stringvar => tkinter.StringVar() holds text that widgets can share; set it with .set() and read it with .get(), and a Label with textvariable= updates by itself.
what does asyncio.run do in python | python asyncio run | how do i use asyncio.run => asyncio.run(main()) starts the event loop, runs the async function main until it finishes, then closes the loop. Call it once at the top of your program.
what does asyncio.sleep do in python | python asyncio sleep | how do i use asyncio.sleep => await asyncio.sleep(1) pauses an async function for 1 second without blocking other tasks, unlike time.sleep.
what does asyncio.gather do in python | python asyncio gather | how do i use asyncio.gather => await asyncio.gather(a(), b()) runs several coroutines at the same time and returns all their results in a list.
what does asyncio.create_task do in python | python asyncio create task | how do i use asyncio.create_task => asyncio.create_task(coro()) schedules a coroutine to run in the background and returns a Task you can await later.
what does asyncio.wait_for do in python | python asyncio wait for | how do i use asyncio.wait_for => await asyncio.wait_for(coro(), timeout=5) gives up with TimeoutError if the coroutine takes longer than 5 seconds.
what does asyncio.queue do in python | python asyncio queue | how do i use asyncio.queue => asyncio.Queue passes items between async tasks safely: await q.put(x) in one task and await q.get() in another.
what does asyncio.taskgroup do in python | python asyncio taskgroup | how do i use asyncio.taskgroup => async with asyncio.TaskGroup() as tg: (Python 3.11+) starts several tasks with tg.create_task and waits for all of them, cancelling the rest if one fails.
what does datetime.minyear do in python | python datetime minyear | how do i use datetime.minyear => datetime.MINYEAR and datetime.MAXYEAR are the smallest and largest years datetime supports, 1 and 9999.
what does random.triangular do in python | python random triangular | how do i use random.triangular => random.triangular(low, high, mode) gives a random float that is more likely to be near mode.
what does random.getrandbits do in python | python random getrandbits | how do i use random.getrandbits => random.getrandbits(k) returns a random integer made of k random bits.
what does pathlib.purepath do in python | python pathlib purepath | how do i use pathlib.purepath => pathlib.PurePath handles path text without touching the disk, useful for splitting and joining paths. Path adds real file operations.
# tag: coding.python.libraries
what does requests.get do in python | python requests get | how do i use requests.get => requests.get(url) downloads a web page or API result. Check r.status_code, then read r.text or r.json(). Install it with pip install requests.
what does requests.post do in python | python requests post | how do i use requests.post => requests.post(url, json=data) sends data to a server, as many web APIs expect.
what does requests.session do in python | python requests session | how do i use requests.session => requests.Session() reuses the connection and cookies across many requests, which is faster for talking to the same site.
what does requests.exceptions do in python | python requests exceptions | how do i use requests.exceptions => requests.exceptions holds errors like ConnectionError and Timeout. Pass timeout=10 to requests.get so it does not wait forever.
what does numpy.array do in python | python numpy array | how do i use numpy.array => numpy.array([1, 2, 3]) makes a fast array. Math works on every element at once, so arr * 2 doubles them all. Most people import numpy as np.
what does numpy.zeros do in python | python numpy zeros | how do i use numpy.zeros => numpy.zeros((3, 4)) makes a 3 by 4 array filled with zeros; numpy.ones does the same with ones.
what does numpy.arange do in python | python numpy arange | how do i use numpy.arange => numpy.arange(0, 10, 2) makes an array like range: 0, 2, 4, 6, 8.
what does numpy.linspace do in python | python numpy linspace | how do i use numpy.linspace => numpy.linspace(0, 1, 5) makes 5 evenly spaced numbers from 0 to 1, including both ends.
what does numpy.mean do in python | python numpy mean | how do i use numpy.mean => numpy.mean(arr) gives the average of an array. There are also numpy.sum, numpy.max, numpy.min and numpy.std.
what does numpy.reshape do in python | python numpy reshape | how do i use numpy.reshape => numpy.reshape(arr, (2, 3)), or arr.reshape(2, 3), changes an array's shape without changing its data.
what does numpy.dot do in python | python numpy dot | how do i use numpy.dot => numpy.dot(a, b) multiplies vectors or matrices. For matrices you can also write a @ b.
what does numpy.random do in python | python numpy random | how do i use numpy.random => numpy.random.default_rng() makes a random generator: rng.integers(1, 7, size=10) rolls ten dice.
what does numpy.where do in python | how do i use numpy.where => numpy.where(arr > 0, arr, 0) picks values element by element: keep positives, replace the rest with 0.
what does numpy.concatenate do in python | python numpy concatenate | how do i use numpy.concatenate => numpy.concatenate([a, b]) joins arrays end to end.
what does pandas.dataframe do in python | python pandas dataframe | how do i use pandas.dataframe => pandas.DataFrame is a table with labelled rows and columns, like a spreadsheet in Python. Most people import pandas as pd.
what does pandas.series do in python | python pandas series | how do i use pandas.series => pandas.Series is one labelled column of data, what you get from df['score'].
what does pandas.read_csv do in python | python pandas read csv | how do i use pandas.read_csv => pandas.read_csv('data.csv') loads a CSV file into a DataFrame. df.head() shows the first rows.
what does pandas.concat do in python | python pandas concat | how do i use pandas.concat => pandas.concat([df1, df2]) stacks DataFrames on top of each other (or side by side with axis=1).
what does pandas.merge do in python | python pandas merge | how do i use pandas.merge => pandas.merge(left, right, on='id') joins two tables where a column matches, like a database join.
what does pandas.to_datetime do in python | python pandas to datetime | how do i use pandas.to_datetime => pandas.to_datetime(df['date']) turns text dates into real dates you can sort and do math with.
what does pil.image.open do in python | python pil.image open | how do i use pil.image.open => PIL.Image.open('photo.png') opens an image with Pillow (pip install pillow). Then img.resize, img.rotate and img.save work on it.
what does pil.image.new do in python | python pil.image new | how do i use pil.image.new => PIL.Image.new('RGB', (200, 100), 'white') makes a blank image you can draw on with PIL.ImageDraw.
